field.name: STEP_TEXT
field.value: <<bb>>Incoming Inspection <</bb>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Verify that the Intel Hitachi chamber stainless steel run card is included inside of the lid of the transit case. Inspect the run card to confirm that the Intel verification section has been signed off by outgoing Intel technicians. Using ESCA/QA, print of a work order for the relevent kit to be refurbished. Also print of a copy of the work order label and place on the transit case the kit was received in. The completed kit must be shipped back in the same transit case. Check all parts for knicks, scratches, and bends to the edges and O-ring sealing surfaces. If any nonconformities are found regarding the run card or with the parts, contact the Production Manager. The procedure for any non conformities found is to use a "yellow tag" process. Once a non conformity is found, note details of this onto the hard copy of the work order, entering as much details as possible such as part name, damage type such a scratch or dent, location of the damage on the part etc. Also state that the part is to be labelled with a "yellow tag" at final inspection. A tracking sheet should be set up to document and capture all "yellow tag" non conformities found. All nonconformities need to be relayed to the tool/part owner for disposition. Once disposition is obtained, the tracking sheet should be populated with this information. This tracking sheet can then be referenced each time the kit/parts are sent of refurbishment and that the same parts does not need to be "yellow tagged" each time its received and inspected. Check shipping case for damage inlcuding castors, latches, hinges or other damage. Report any damage found to Production Manager. All parts within a kit shall be processed as a batch and not mixed with another kit.

field.name: STEP_TEXT
field.value: <<bb>>Planar Polish <</bb>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Tool: FT Sponge , Palm sander <<nl/>>Abrasive: Med scotchbrite/ Foamtec <<nl/>>Finish: Random brush <<nl/>> <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Manual polish of the wet part after the DI Water is required to physically remove any incoming surface deposits before acid bath treatment. Use the maroon (medium) scotch brite scrub as required at the edges of all parts to remove the deposits at the edge ONLY. Use on the flat regions of the part only if presence of thick deposits are observed. The manual polish of the flat regions is done using a two-step method: 800 grit followed by 1350 grit Foamtec Pads. This two-step process is required to remove any visible color variation or other non-conformities. The incoming dents or scratches during part handling will not be removed by the planar polish step and should be documented before the start of planar polish. During the planar polish process, DI Water should be used frequently to remove the polish debris. Also, the polish pads should be supported by polish sponge on the flat regions, and the polishing done in an orbital pattern.

<<bb>>Primary Packaging <</bb>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Type: vacuum seal <<nl/>>Package: poly bag <<nl/>>Environment: Class-100 <<nl/>>Vacuum: >5" Hg <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Single bag vacuum seal all parts. Place ESCAQA part number / serial sticker on first bag. Double bag vacuum seal first bag and all parts.
All Stainless Steel parts should be vacuum sealed after the part has reached the temperature of 20-25 C.
If the black protective edge covers are supplied with the 3 piece kits for the Grounded Electrode, please ensure that the edge cover is wiped down using 6% IPA soaked Texwipe. Proceed to blow off the edge protector with CDA. Once cleaned, attach the edge protector to the Groundede Electrode. Note: Do not use 100% IPA to wipe these as it damages the material of the edge protector.
For transcontinental shipping, after vacuum sealing as described above, moisture seal using mylar vapor bags should also be done. This is essential to prevent moisture leakage into the vacuum sealed bags.

Secondary Packaging
Use the same transit case the kit was received in, which should have a corresponding work order number label from incoming inspection to help you identify it. Place all kit parts into the shipping case for transport. Complete final run card entries as necessary and prepare MSR-FSR shipping documents. Take note of part numbers stamped on parts and ensure throttle valve plate pairs are properly accounted for.
